title: Introduce autogenic palette bridges and modular radius anchors for forms and charts
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Replace the current ad-hoc color ramps and scattered radius values used by forms, tables, and charts with a cohesive, autogenic palette bridging system and a small set of modular radius anchors. This work reduces CSS/token churn, improves contrast consistency across components, and enables a predictable migration path for product owners and platform engineers.

Scope:
- Define a 12-stop palette bridge pattern (core -> ambient) that automates perceptual steps between accent and neutral ramps for light/dark modes.
- Establish 3 modular radius anchors (compact, standard, spacious) with explicit mapping to existing components (buttons, inputs, cards, table cells, chart tooltips).
- Update typography tokens that interact with spacing/radius (minor kerning/letter-spacing deltas for small and large label sizes) to avoid visual crowding at new densities.
- Produce migration guidelines, codemods, and a phased rollout plan with visual-diff gating.

Deliverables: token spec (yaml/json), Figma token library, Storybook stories, Chromatic visual-diff baseline, migration runbook, and one engineering PR to wire tokens into the component library.

Trade-offs considered:
- Fewer radius anchors simplify CSS and performance (fewer stylesheet branches) but require compromises in some legacy layouts; we've chosen 3 anchors to balance flexibility and migration cost.
- Autogenic bridges reduce manual color pair tuning but can produce edge cases for extreme brand accents; we'll ship a small set of manual overrides for brand-critical screens.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Tokens exist as JSON with clear naming, semantic intent, and light/dark variants.
- All updated components show <= 2 visual regressions (reviewed and triaged) in Chromatic.
- Accessibility: color contrast meets WCAG AA for normal text and >= AA for UI components; a checklist for AAA scenarios included.
- Migration runbook validated by 2 product teams and one internal platform integration (Dedicated Console).

migration_plan: Phase 1 (tokens only): land token JSON + Figma update, no component changes. Phase 2 (components behind flag): wire tokens into input/button/card; run Chromatic and manual QA. Phase 3 (gradual rollout): enable feature flag by product teams, provide codemod for legacy token names, and monitor visual-diff dashboard for regressions. Provide rollback path by toggling shim layer. Estimated timeline: 3 sprints.
